correctness.rationale: Adjunction, nefness of -K and Cauchy–Schwarz show that the thirteen explicitly listed curves are the entire geometric negative-curve set, including all (-1) and (-2) curves. A Schur complement proves the graph criterion for negative definiteness. The Zariski chamber-to-support bijection and the descended ample-plus-effective construction show arithmetic invariant supports equal ground-field realizable chambers. Exact independent graph and integer determinant verifiers enumerate all 8192 subsets and 24 group actions; both match the five polynomial vectors. Two independent Burnside/direct orbit calculations give the same 61 orbits and size distribution. The computation is finite and exhaustive by the proven negative-curve classification; it is not inferred from finite-field sampling.

value.rationale: Cayley’s four-nodal cubic is the unique maximally nodal cubic, and its four node Galois forms exhaust a natural arithmetic family. The five Zariski-chamber distributions classify stable negative supports of rational big divisor classes; the two order-two types are separated by 66 versus 74 chambers even though their single-curve orbit-size partitions agree. The full 61-orbit decomposition gives an additional structural classification useful for arithmetic divisor theory and computation on singular cubic resolutions; the result goes beyond the already known 726 geometric chambers and open-surface point counts.
